subject: MSA + Order Form: Clarify Output Ownership & Training Opt-out (TechNova)
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha@technova.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: Clarify Output Ownership & Training Opt-out (TechNova)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion I’m attaching the latest MSA and the draft Order Form with the TechNova redlines dropped in (attachment: TechNova_MSARedlines_20260924.pdf). Two quick asks so we can keep the procurement timetable intact:

- Can you confirm whether TechNova intends to request an absolute prohibition on model training using customer content, or an opt-out that Redwood would honor upon request for specific products?
- There are three customer-driven edits in the Order Form around "Output Ownership" and "Feedback License" that look like they could be narrowed to product-scoped carveouts rather than company-wide rights. Would your team accept product-bound language?

High-level context for your legal team: Redwood’s standard approach is to provide customers ownership of their outputs and a limited feedback license for model improvement, with an explicit training opt-out available on request for hosted deployments. For private/dedicated deployments, customers typically control training entirely. We’re happy to document stronger limits for TechNova if that’s required, but it will affect the SLA/price for hosted consumption.

I’m looping in Karthik from Product and Laura from Sales Ops to help map the technical and billing implications while we route the redlines. If it’s easier, we can set a short call between legal teams later today.

Next steps: If you can flag must-have language and optional asks in TechNova’s redlines, I’ll coordinate an internal legal response and propose compromise text.

Thanks —

Ava Chen

Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Clarify Output Ownership & Training Opt-out (TechNova)

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the doc. We’d like to be explicit: TechNova requires that Redwood not use TechNova content to train models that could serve other customers without an explicit written opt-in. We’re open to a carveout that permits aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement, but anything that could regenerate customer-specific outputs must be excluded.

Key asks from our side:
1) Output Ownership: Customer owns outputs generated from their prompts; Redwood must show provenance if requested.
2) Training/Feedback: No training on TechNova data without written consent; limited telemetry ok for stability/bug fixes.
3) Feedback License: If Redwood asks for a general feedback license, it should be non-exclusive, revocable, and scoped to pseudonymized telemetry only.

Attached is a redline PDF with proposed language. We need to close the Order Form by the end of next week (10/1) to align with TechNova’s procurement window.

Please route to your legal team and let me know if they want a call.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA + Order Form: Clarify Output Ownership & Training Opt-out (TechNova)

Ava / team —

Thanks for the ping and the redlines. I reviewed TechNova’s proposed language and suggest the following path forward that is defensible and commercially acceptable:

Summary of our position and recommended tradeoffs:
- Output Ownership: We can accept explicit language that customers own outputs generated from their content. We'll include a short provenance clause (internal logs + timestamps) and a customer request process for exports; this does not create a license back to the customer.
- Training / Feedback License: Offer a two-tier approach:
  1) Hosted API: Provide a firm "no-training" option where TechNova can elect (in the Order Form) to opt their account out of Redwood’s training pipelines entirely. This opt-out will be implemented operationally and will be priced as a premium add-on.
  2) Dedicated / Private: For dedicated capacity or on-prem customers, Redwood will confirm that customer data remains under their control and will not be used for shared model training unless explicitly contracted.
- Telemetry & Service Improvement: We can permit collection of aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry for stability, bug fixes, latency improvements, and quality monitoring. Make this explicit and state that such telemetry will not be used to train base models that could reproduce customer outputs.
- Feedback License Mechanics: Replace a perpetual, global feedback license with a revocable, non-exclusive feedback license limited to "pseudonymized telemetry and aggregated metrics" and expressly exclude customer prompts and outputs.

Draft language (two short clauses to put in the Order Form):
1) Customer Outputs: "Customer retains ownership of Outputs generated from Customer Content. Upon Customer request Redwood will provide reasonable export of provenance logs and copies of Outputs."
2) Training & Feedback: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train models that are subsequently served to other customers, unless Redwood receives Customers prior written consent. Customer may elect an additional 'No-Training' option in the Order Form for hosted deployments; this option will be implemented operationally and may incur additional fees. Redwood may collect and use aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry for operational improvement, but such telemetry will not include Customers raw prompts or Outputs and will not be used to train models that can reproduce Customer-specific Outputs."

I believe this preserves TechNova’s core asks while giving Redwood practical operational language. Karthik — please give a quick note on cost delta for a hosted "No-Training" opt-out (rough percent uplift or flat fee) so I can include it in the response. Laura — can you prepare an Order Form snippet and pricing placeholder we can attach?

If TechNova insists on a company-wide prohibition without an Order Form opt-in path, we should escalate to the exec sponsor; that will materially change pricing and limits our R&D usage for service improvements.

Happy to jump on a short call with TechNova counsel to run through the draft.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0160

Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Clarify Output Ownership & Training Opt-out (TechNova)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for flagging procurement timelines. Per our internal review (see Marissas summary below) we can offer the following compromise:

1) Output Ownership: Confirmed — TechNova owns Outputs. Redwood will provide provenance logs on request.
2) Training / Feedback: We can implement a "No-Training" opt-out you select in the Order Form for hosted services. This prevents TechNova content from being used to train Redwoods shared models. It will be reflected as an add-on line item in the Order Form (pricing placeholder attached). For Dedicated/Private deployments, we confirm that customer data will not be used for shared training unless explicitly contracted.
3) Telemetry: Redwood may collect aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts) for service stability/bug fixes; we will exclude raw prompts and Outputs from training datasets.

Attached is a short redline that replaces broad feedback-license language with a revocable, telemetry-limited license and includes the Order Form checkbox for the No-Training option (attachment: Redwood_Resp_Proposal_v2.docx). Can you confirm if that aligns with TechNovas legal team? If yes, well prepare a DocuSign packet with the Order Form + MSA and send for signature; target timeline = week of 9/28.

If you prefer a synchronous discussion, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow (Tues) at 9am PT.

Best regards,

Ava Chen
